title: Send and 'static: crossing boundaries
summary: Work that moves to another thread or task must own its data (or share it atomically).
lecture: thread::spawn (and multithreaded task spawning) accepts closures that are Send + 'static: nothing borrowed from the current stack frame — because the thread may outlive it (E0373). The `move` keyword is usually the fix: give the closure ownership.

Send means 'safe to hand to another thread'. Most types are; the notable civilian exception is Rc — its reference count isn't atomic, so two threads bumping it is a data race. Arc is the same idea with atomic counting, and it IS Send.

The async twist: a future remembers every local it holds ACROSS an .await. Hold an Rc across an await point and the whole future becomes !Send — unusable on a multithreaded executor (E0277 pointing at the spawn). Fix by switching to Arc, or by dropping the non-Send value before the await.
Reflex: at every spawn boundary, ask 'who owns this data, and can it cross?' — move it, Arc it, or finish with it first.

example.caption: What crosses the boundary must be owned — and atomically shareable.
